notes.title: Scene State and Transition 💾
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=KEKVjkaS_h4;full][/previewyoutube]

It's New Zealand screenshot Saturday! 📣 

But I usually post a video hehe 🤭

Today, I’m showcasing a transition from one world scene to another. While it might seem simple, scene transitions are actually complex.

For example, when we run a scene in Godot, the states of objects reset upon transitioning.

Our goal is to ensure that previous scene states are retained when we return. If I cut down a tree or empty a chest in one scene, I want the changes to persist when we come back. World events, like our world clock, should also continue from the time we left the scene.

The past few weeks have been exhausting as I’ve been working on efficiently saving states between scenes. Currently, this state-saving is happening in-memory, but I plan to save states into a file soon.

That’s it for today! Thanks for all your feedback, suggestions and support 😊

notes.title: Inventory system ~ Gem container 💎
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=RgaTx5CUA3c;full][/previewyoutube]

Hello again! Hope everyone is doing great. It's March already and autumn just arrived here in New Zealand! Another season, another Mahika update 💪

Been working hard getting the inventory system up and running, and the second part is now done and dusted. 👨‍🔧

We now have a working inventory layout and separated the inventory panel into 3 sections:
[list]
[*] Hotbar
[*] Item container and
[*] Gem container
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43049997/f179838cfb0fef07bb4d3e7fef95b7a1134afe78.png[/img]

Items that can be equipped will first try to go to the Hotbar. Then all gems go to the Gem container. And everything else that can't go to the Hotbar or Gem container will end up in the Item container if there are slots available.

Then, we repurposed the previously named "Gem panel" to become the "Magic panel".

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43049997/7ed32cefd8bb2d5efe66e86d5c2c1c77f699286a.png[/img]

This Magic panel will show the equipped gem at the bottom slot, then show the available magic at the other slots, and then equip the first tier magic when the gem is equipped.

The inventory can be accessed by pressing "i" in the keyboard. It will slide up and down including the Hotbar.

The Magic panel's hot keys, to equip magic and gem, were also re-mapped to make it closer to the default player movement keys.
[list]
[*] Q ~ 1st tier magic
[*] R ~ 2nd tier magic
[*] E ~ 3rd tier magic
[*] CTRL ~ Equip/Cycle between gems in the gem container
[/list]

Gems will be our main catalyst for magic. All magic will be available through gems.

Lastly, we fixed a bug that causes the cool down magic effect to reset when equipping a new gem.

That's it! More inventory system updates to come.

Thanks again for watching/reading the vlog/blog. We appreciate all your helpful feedback!

Stay safe and always have fun!

[*] Character movement and animation now complete
[*] Character attack animation now complete
[*] Tilemap structure now complete with better understanding on how Godot arranges tiles and the features it provides
[*] Enemy simple chase player AI now complete
[/list]
Thanks to [url=https://www.facebook.com/dythrw]Dyethrow PIXEL[/url] for the awesome pixel art.

notes.title: New Game Engine and Updated Title
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43049997/8b500d535de5af199c58a27eb51ec686053201fd.gif[/img]

You may have heard about the Unity pricing issues 3 weeks ago. With that, we came to a decision to [url=https://candycabinets.com/2023/09/16/mahika-is-moving-to-godot/]move to Godot[/url]. Many Unity game developers decided to wait out the storm and they got the concession. But even if Unity management decided to step back on the pricing scheme, we're still sticking to Godot especially now that we already have a good feel on what this open source engine can offer.

We started porting the game for over 2 weeks now and we're loving the process! There are lots of tutorials online and Godot fits our pixel art style. The engine is very good when it comes to rendering and scaling pixel art. It's also an easy game engine to learn so we're confident we can get back on track with our development.

We also wanted to announce that the game will no longer take the subtitle "Prologue" and will only use [b]Mahika[/b] as its title. With this, the game will be released as a paid game and we will upload a separate Demo version.

That's it for now. Stay tuned as we churn up more artwork and game updates!

notes.title: Procedural Dungeon Levels
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=gMPTcJTzN6g;full][/previewyoutube]

It's been a while but we're back with exciting updates on Mahika : Prologue!

First off, we got sidelined for a bit, but now back on track! However, we had to move Mahika’s release date for next year.

All is good now as we’re starting to gain momentum again as we finished one important feature of the game ~ Procedural Level Generation!

It was a fiddly task as we had to experiment with a couple of procedural patterns and redrawing the dungeon walls. In the end, it looks awesome!

Dungeon levels are not much at this stage as we still work on procedural content generation. But expect a livelier update in the coming weeks once we chuck in the decorations, treasures, breakable items, and enemies!

Hope you stay tune for more updates.

Stay safe and always have fun!

The load character screen now looks consistent with the other screens, taking inspiration from other load character screen designs.

We added the new character builder to the sequence. And we updated the graphics of the popup dialogue screens.

We still have a couple of screens to update and we're re-organizing the Game and Level scenes. 

Hope you stay tune for more updates.
